data.long_meaning: Goddess who gives life and nourishment. The name Pranusha carries the meaning “Giver of Life” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Pranusha usually hope their child will grow to embody giver of life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child believed to be a blessing from the gods, symbolizing the life force and vitality of the universe
data.etymology: Pranusha belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giver of Life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pranusha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pranusha holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, where it is connected to the goddess of life and nourishment, Prana Devi. Prana Devi is believed to be the embodiment of prana or life force, which sustains all living beings. This name is also reminiscent of the importance given to life and health in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Pranusha is a name that symbolizes the divine essence that grants life and sustains it. It is a reminder of the spiritual truth that life is not just a material existence but a manifestation of the divine. The name holds a deep spiritual significance, evoking a sense of reverence and gratitude towards the divine power that gives life and nourishment to all beings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pranusha: Embodiment of the vital life force (Prana) and inner awakening (Shakti). She nurtures and enlivens, inspiring self-realization and inner transformation.

historical_references.reference: Pranusha is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. She was the wife of Bhishma, the grandsire of the Pandavas and Kauravas. Pranusha was a voracious eater and was cursed by the sage Vyasa for eating the food meant for the sage Markandeya during a yajna. The curse made Pranusha immortal but also caused her to be burned every time the sun rose. Eventually, she was relieved of her suffering by Bhishma by requesting him to shield her from the sun.

In another reference, Pranusha is considered an aspect of the goddess Durga. She is depicted as the goddess of food and nourishment. Pranusha is also known as Annapurna (the one who is full of food). She is often invoked during prayers for the prosperity and well-being of households.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Pranusha has recently gained popularity beyond traditional Indian contexts, as it is being used as a hashtag on Instagram for posts related to mental health and self-care among Indian women. On YouTube, there are several videos exploring the deeper meaning and symbolism of the name Pranusha, particularly in the context of feminist interpretations of Indian mythology. On Reddit, there is a growing community dedicated to discussing the significance of Pranusha in modern Hinduism and exploring ways to incorporate her story into contemporary spiritual practices.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Pranusha, a teacher in Kathmandu, Nepal, shares that their name Pranusha meaning "Giver of Life" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
